title: Reliability and quality assessment of internet videos as guidance for dietary weight loss intervention: a cross-sectional study in China
screen_reason: QUALITY-ONLY study (§1 exclusion ground, cross-referenced to §3). The 300 videos (top 100 for the keyword 'dietary weight loss' on BiliBili, Douyin/TikTok and Kwai, 28 Feb 2024) were scored ONLY with the Global Quality Score (GQS, 1-5 for flow, ease of understanding, overall usefulness) and modified DISCERN (0-5 for clarity, reliability, fairness, references, rigor). No item is ever judged true or false against an external ground truth: there is no fact-check, no expert veracity verification, no guideline-concordance accurate/inaccurate coding, no explicit false/misleading label and no source-reliability list. Results are reported exclusively as means and medians of those scales (all means 1.70-2.04, all medians 2), never as a share of videos containing misinformation, so there is no quantitative share with a denominator to extract - the 'A Likert scale reported only as a mean is not a share' rule applies. The word misinformation appears only as an inference the authors draw from low scores ('the prevalence of low-quality videos ... exposes viewers to significant risks of misinformation'), not as a measured quantity. A wholly accurate video can score 1-2 here for being short, unreferenced or one-sided, which is the §3 test for QUALITY rather than CONTENT.
missed_or_uncertain: Nothing extractable was left behind, but every quality figure is recorded here so an adjudicator can promote it to a QUALITY row in one step if this project's convention is to keep such rows (§3 says 'row kept, excluded from prevalence', while §1 lists QUALITY-ONLY studies as an exclusion ground; I followed §1 plus the schema line 'empty list if EXCLUDE'). The would-be QUALITY rows, all China, keyword 饮食减重 ('dietary weight loss'), searched 28 February 2024, n = 100 videos per platform (300 total), value_kind scale_score, professional raters: BiliBili GQS mean 2.04, median 2 (range 0-4); BiliBili mDISCERN mean 2.01, median 2 (range 0-5); Douyin/TikTok GQS mean 1.81, median 2 (range 1-3); Douyin/TikTok mDISCERN mean 1.81, median 2 (range 0-3); Kwai/Kuaishou GQS mean 1.70, median 2 (range 1-3); Kwai/Kuaishou mDISCERN mean 1.73, median 2 (range 0-3). Verbatim: 'the average GQS scores for dietary weight loss videos on BiliBili, TikTok, and Kwai were 2.04, 1.81, and 1.70, respectively, while the average mDISCERN scores were 2.01, 1.81, and 1.73. The median scores for both GQS and mDISCERN across the three platforms were 2.' Other unextracted material: (a) the same videos rescored by three non-medical raters (GQS 2.10 / 2.29 / 2.77; mDISCERN 1.67 / 1.91 / 2.41 for BiliBili / TikTok / Kwai) with Cohen's kappa between professional and lay ratings below 0.2 (highest 0.19 GQS BiliBili; per-dimension range 0.43 for BiliBili Clarity down to -0.09 for TikTok Reliability) - still scale scores, and interesting mainly as evidence that the instrument is not measuring anything a lay viewer recognises; (b) subgroup means by uploader (doctor vs non-doctor, e.g. BiliBili 1.56 vs 2.13 GQS) and by content category (Table 5, e.g. TikTok advertisements GQS 1.00) - again means, not shares; (c) composition counts that are shares of the corpus but not of misinformation: doctor-uploaded videos 18/100 BiliBili, 5/100 TikTok, 20/100 Kwai; 'weight loss knowledge' 49/100, 48/100, 56/100; personal experience 30/100, 50/100, 27/100; advertisements 9/100, 2/100, 15/100. These are creator/genre composition, not veracity, so they are not prevalence estimates; (d) correlations (GQS with duration r = 0.41; GQS with likes r = -0.18, etc.) and regression coefficients - associations, not shares; (e) the cited 9.7 billion views of #weightloss TikTok videos and comparison GQS values from other studies (thyroid cancer 3.72, liver cancer median 3, IBD 2.61, post-bariatric nutrition 2.35) are borrowed from other papers, barred by R8.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content assessment of algorithmically ranked video samples, no human subjects (ethical review not required). Single keyword 饮食减重 ('dietary weight loss', operationally defined as caloric restriction, macronutrient changes, meal replacements or time-restricted eating; exercise-only, bariatric-surgery and prescription-drug videos excluded) searched on one day, 28 February 2024, on BiliBili 7.68.0, Douyin/TikTok 28.6.0 and Kwai 12.0.40, from newly created accounts to blunt personalisation; results left in each platform's default recommendation order, duplicates removed, serial videos merged, and the top 100 eligible videos per platform retained (N = 300). Publisher credentials verified against hospital websites where claimed. Instruments: GQS (1-5) and mDISCERN (0-5), translated into Chinese, with a 10-video pilot calibration. Blinding: platform watermarks blurred, raters blind to engagement metrics and source. Three primary clinician raters (JS, QZ, ZS) scored every video; unanimous scores stood, one-point spreads resolved by majority, wider spreads reassessed by two secondary raters (FS, RX) and, if still discordant, settled in discussion by a tertiary grader (YZ). Inter-rater agreement among the three primary raters: all Fleiss' kappa > 0.90 (GQS 0.90 / 0.95 / 0.98; mDISCERN 0.90 / 0.93 / 0.94). A parallel non-medical rater panel (QL, SY, ZX) repeated the scoring; professional-vs-lay Cohen's kappa < 0.2 throughout. Statistics: Shapiro-Wilk, Mann-Whitney U, Spearman correlations, per-platform multivariable linear regression; no correction for multiple comparisons, which the authors acknowledge inflates Type I error. Authors' stated limitations: top-100 algorithmic selection bias, a single keyword, a single-day snapshot, Chinese platforms only, and no user-outcome data. Raw data available from the authors on request; no funding.
rob.item6_quote: We utilized the mDISCERN and the Global Quality Score (GQS) tools to assess the reliability and informational quality of the videos, respectively, the validity of which has been confirmed in previous studies (25-27).
rob.item10_quote: We identified the top 100 dietary weight-loss videos on each platform in February 2024, resulting in a total of 300 videos.
